title: Counting-sort placement phase
statement: Let a counting-sort input have $n$ items $x_i$ with keys $k_i<N$, stored at source address $s$, with a destination range and $N+1$ counter cells satisfying the required bounds and disjointness conditions; assume the key cells are also within the address bound and disjoint from both ranges. Suppose the counter memory has cumulative counts $\#\{i<n:k_i<t\}$ at counter $t$ for $t\le N$, and bucket sizes $\#\{i<n:k_i=t\}$ at counter $t+1$ for $t<N$. From any state with loop index $r$, arbitrary other loop variables, and memory agreeing with the initial memory outside the destination and counter ranges, the placement program has an execution of cost at most $38n+6$ ending with loop index $n$, memory still agreeing outside those ranges, updated counters encoding the next positions, and each processed item $j<n$ stored at its stable sorted position.
hypotheses_covered: Counting-sort preconditions: word bound, source/destination/counter bounds, item and key contents, key range, and required interval disjointness
Initial memory has cumulative counts through bucket $N$ and bucket sizes from bucket $r$ onward
Initial state has the specified loop-index frame and agrees with initial memory outside destination and counter ranges
caveat: The counter invariant and state predicate are bundled formal definitions; the given descriptions do not define them.
